title: South Korea, Japan buffeted by hacks as AI lowers bar for cybercriminals
source_used: Reuters text as carried by KELO-AM (kelo.com) (read in full); Reuters page returned HTTP 401
key_facts: Nine South Korean banks and two mega-churches are probing cyberattacks that may have involved AI tools; Japanese firms including Daiwa Securities, SoftBank Corp and Lawson have been hit by a surge in incidents.
Authorities are still investigating whether and how AI was used in many of the breaches.

CrowdStrike said a suspected 26-year-old China-based attacker behind the Korean bank incidents probably could not have carried out the campaign without AI assistance, using a Chinese-developed AI agent and Anthropic's Claude Code.
Japan recorded more cybersecurity incidents in the first nine months of the year than in all of last year, per TrendAI; incidents rose to 86 in September.
South Korea reported 1,236 cyber incidents in the first half of the year, up 20% from a year earlier.

South Korea's Financial Services Commission ordered financial bodies and affected executives to complete a 12-point cybersecurity self-assessment; Japan's digital transformation minister convened ministries on Thursday.
Fitch's Karen Wu expects regulatory penalties, customer compensation costs and higher security spending, and said losses were not yet material.
